description: Every corpus token that is one sign or a combination of signs (a ligature, a vessel sign, a logogram, or a logogram joined to a sign) and has no entry in the lexicon, with its attestations and what is on file for it. The sister of unread_words.json, which holds words of two or more signs. Hand-edited.

statuses.component_read: a combined sign with a component the lexicon reads
statuses.value_on_file: sign_values.json or a translation gives it a value; it has no lexicon entry

kinds.logogram: a logogram named by its Latin code
kinds.compound: a logogram or sign joined to others by a hyphen

excluded.None: a placeholder in the corpus record, not a sign
excluded.double mina: a metrological notation, spelled out in the corpus
excluded.𐁁: a Linear B glyph in the corpus record

entries.note: Alone on 25 Haghia Triada nodules (HT Wa 1150–1174) and on the metal object HT Zf 165. On tablets it stands as an entry between dividers before a grain logogram: HT 115a *47-NU-RA-JA · I · GRA+BOSm, HT 43 MA-SI-DU · PA-*342-I · I · GRA+PA 5; before OLIV 1 on ZA 11b. No reading.

Alone on 12 Haghia Triada nodules (HT Wa 1267–1278). On tablets an entry with a quantity: TA 4 before the total on HT 94a and HT 109, TA 6 on HT 154a, TA 2 on KH 8; TA 4 on the Thera stone object THE Zg 5. No reading.

Alone on 3 Haghia Triada nodules (HT Wa 1147–1149) and the Petras vessel PE Zb 8. One tablet keeps it whole as an entry: HT 37 .5 A 15 under KI-RO, the 15 dotted and the half-line written over an erasure (GORILA I 71). No reading. Every other tablet breaks at the sign: A[ on HT 57a .2 (I 111), KH 45 .1 (III 71), ARKH 1b .1 (III 5) and ZA 21a .7, there dotted (III 195); ]A[ on PH 27 .2 (I 313); A-[ on ARKH 5 .3, where the editors allow A-DA[ (III 17). KH 17 .4 and KH 33 .2 break straight after a dotted A (III 49, 63), and on KH 73 .1 breaks after a dotted A and .3 has A, a dash and the break (III 91). The fraction once read after A on HT 57a stands on the next line, broken at both sides. The A before SA-SA-RA-ME on PK Za 11 is the first sign of A-SA-SA-RA-ME and is counted with that word.
Alone on 11 Khania roundels and 3 Haghia Triada nodules (HT Wa 1279–1281); on the roundel KN Wc 42 beside a face that reads ]-NA. With a quantity on HT 113: O 2½. No reading.

Alone on 12 Khania roundels in the corpus (KH Wc 2036–2045, 2095, 2111). Inside a word at Haghia Triada: RA-*164-TI (HT 17, HT 19). Nosch and Weilhartner take it as a syllabogram at Haghia Triada and a logogram at Khania, possibly for textiles, because a similar sign is a textile logogram in Linear B, *164, known only at Knossos (2026), one of the cloths Nosch says 'may be Minoan textile types' (2024, 341). No reading.
Alone on 9 Khania roundels (KH Wc 2046–2053, 2113) and the Armenoi stone object ARM Zg 1. *301 with *311 attached; the lexicon reads *301. No reading.

The [?] is an element joined to the hide sign that the transcription does not name; no sign is lost. At Malia the drawings show a cross inside the sign on MA 6a and an angle beside it on MA 6c. At Phaistos the sign of PH 10 has the hide's outline and that of PH 15b is nearer an animal's head.

Whole on the metal object CR Zf 5 and before a numeral on PK 3 (JA 20), a bar whose script is doubted. Elsewhere the corpus record sets a break beside it: on both sides on the stone vessel AP Za 3 and on ZA 32, after it on SY Za 1 (I-DA-MI · JA-[), and before it on HT 44b (]JA · TE-GRA+F) and PH 1a (]JA · *316 1). No reading.

No token of NA alone survives whole. HT 64 .2 ]NA 2 and ARKH 1b .4 ]⟦NA 8⟧, the second in erasure brackets, are broken before NA (GORILA I 119; III 5). KH 36 .2 ]-NA[ ends a broken word (GORILA III 65), as does ]-NA on the second face of KN Wc 42. HT 154 C .1 ]NA-[ opens one, 'probablement' NA-MI[ (GORILA I 245).

The NA that opens side b of KN Za 10 is the last sign of JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA and is counted with that word.

Whole on KH 47 alone, where RA · *306 opens the last line at the preserved left edge, and in its own panel on the ring KN Zg 57b, between WI and KA. A break precedes RA on HT 147, KH 29 and ZA 11b (]RA 2), and follows it on HT 53a; on KH 14 (RA · A-MA-JA · CYP 6) the drawing does not show the left margin intact. No reading.
HT 11b *86 · KA 40 opens a list counted in KA. Uchitel takes the sign for a schematic ship, heading shipments (2016b, 9); the syllabic value proposed is na. No lexicon entry.

Alone on the nodule KN Wa 51. The tablets hold no whole token: KH 9 .2 MI[ is broken after MI (GORILA III 35), ZA 20 .2 ]MI[ has traces of three signs after it (GORILA III 193), and HT 113ter sets MI over 4 on a fragment whose surface is lost beside the sign.

Alone before a number in the commodity slot: HT 132 A-SE · *319 5; HT Zd 156 *319 2¼ and *319 3⅜, each figure half again the one before. It closes MA-TI-TI on HT Zd 155 and HT Zd 157. A plain I-beam, a stem with a bar at top and bottom; 'a probable transaction sign' on HT 132 (Steele 2024, 103). No reading.

On HT Zd 156 the first two counts follow a sign GORILA reads as 24, NE, each dotted (IV 133); Schrijver (2014, 14) and Corazza et al. (2021, 3) print *319 before all four. The series 1, 1½, 2¼, 3⅜, 5¹⁄₁₆ is a sum growing by half each term with the interest joined to the capital (CAD Ṣ 159–160, s.v. ṣibtu A), so *319 is the thing reckoned at interest, given on the two graffiti and counted 5 to the physician.

Rival: a punctuation sign. GORILA's corrigenda have 'I p.-ê. ponctuation' for the graffiti (V 80), and Salgarella keeps it open for the two word-final tokens (2020, 332). GORILA indexes the sign of HT 132.1 as a logogram (V 297), where a divider precedes it and 5 follows; its list of punctuation signs also holds the fraction signs 707 and 708 (V 325); and the writer of HT Zd 155 parts A-JU from the next word with a short stroke.

Rival: a string held taut between two pegs, a monochord, or a measured 'unit length', each from the sign's form and the graffito alone (Stieglitz 1978, 129–130); HT 132 counts 5 of it to the physician beside 27 ewes.

Proposed: silver. It is lent at interest, ṯlṯm ksp b nṯk 'thirty shekels of silver of interest' (KTU 4.682:12; DULAT 644), and five shekels of it are the physician's fee for setting a bone (Laws of Hammurabi § 221; CAD A/2 346, s.v. asû A), beside A-SE · *319 5. The proposal rests on that one number; nothing in the sign's form says silver. Copper in the ingot is excluded: the Linear B ingot signs are four-horned (Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 51, fig. 10), and none of the marked ingots of Haghia Triada (HT Zf 163–169) carries the sign.
GORILA A 652, 401VAS+60 (GORILA V 311): whole on KH 31 .2; on KH 91 .4 and MI 2 .3 the reading is dotted and the token stands at a break.

GORILA A 658, 412VAS+E: the jar of *412 with the fraction sign E written inside it, listed again under the fraction (GORILA V 314, 318). Counted 4, 3 and 2 on MA 10. The jar has one handle high at the left, a narrow neck and swelling shoulders, the outline of Linear B *205, a-te-we, 'a straight-sided ewer' (Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 324, 327).
GORILA A 659, 412VAS+F: the jar of *412 with the fraction sign F written inside it, listed again under the fraction (GORILA V 314, 319). Counted 4 and 3 on MA 10, each time after *412+E.
The fraction sign A 709, with no value on file. PH 7b .1 ]TA 1 L and .2 ]DA-RA L, each line broken at the left (GORILA I 295); KN 49 · L, after a divider.

The one token, ZA 21b .7, is erased: ⟦ME⟧, the sign dotted (GORILA III 197). ZA 21a .1 ]ME is broken before ME, with traces there (GORILA III 195).

The ME after JA-SA-SA-RA on IO Za 16 continues that word across the line break (JA-SA-SA-RA-ME) and is counted with it.

On the Akrotiri ostracon THE Zg 5, PU 5 is one of the single signs before quantities taken for abbreviations of Minoan textile names (Michailidou 1992–1993; Boulotis 1998; Burke 2010, 49, apud Nosch and Weilhartner 2026, 131). Linear B writes PU on its cloth sign, 'quite likely the abbreviation of pu-ka-ta-ri-ja, puktaliā', a cloth of double thickness, and the word 'may be linked with πτυκτός' (Killen 2024, 724, 729). If that word is Greek, the ostracon's PU abbreviates another. HT 34 has PU ⅛ after E+KA ¹⁄₁₆, and the graffito KN Zd 46 carries the sign alone.
On THE Zb 13 a doubtful AB 21 stands apart before VIN+TE 120. On the roundels KH Wc 2102 and PH Wc 44 the sign is the sheep logogram, in the lexicon as *21.
Alone on the roundel KN Wc 23. HT 125a .1 and HT 130 .3 have ]RA₂[, the sign dotted and broken on both sides (GORILA I 215, 225), on tablets that also spell SA-RA₂.

Before a commodity: TA₂ before GRA, counted 3, on HT 137, and joined to the cyperus sign as TA₂-CYP on KH 60. HT 11a closes with TA₂ 15, after VIR+[?]-I 3, and KH 29 has RA · TA₂ 1, broken before RA. No word beginning with TA₂ stands before a grain sign: TA₂-TA-RE and TA₂-TI-TE of PK 1 are names counted 1 each.

A logogram alone on ZA 6a.1 (Salgarella 2020, 330), among the Linear A logograms with a possible Linear B homomorph, *171 (Schoep 2002, 131–35, apud Salgarella 2020, 220 n. 119); Nosch and Weilhartner class it among the agricultural commodities (2026, 119). The sign before 7 on the Akrotiri ostracon THE Zg 5 is TE, as Nosch and Weilhartner print it (2026, 131), and the drawings part the two: on ZA 6a the sign has a curved top, a short crossbar under it and an oblique foot; on the ostracon it is a stem with a straight top bar and a crossbar close under it, with no foot. *319 of HT 132 is another sign again: two straight bars and nothing between them.

A logogram counted in whole numbers, twice in one slot of KH Scribe 2: KH 6 .6 ]-RE · *334 1 and KH 7a .1 ]NE-[·]-KI *334 4, dotted there, each before a cyperus fraction (GORILA III 27, 29). In that slot the same hand counts *21M, MU and *306 on KH 6 and VIR+*313b on KH 7a. Salgarella has A 334 as 'logogram?', sign alone (Salgarella 2020, 316).

Neither token stands clear of a break. KH 12 .2 has it over an erasure, between two fractions, with a dotted [ after it (GORILA III 41); KH 44 .2 has ]*335[ in the tabular copy, with traces at the left (III 71).

Drawn as an animal's head facing right, two ovals above it and an eye within. KH 14 .2 *336 2, whole, between two cyperus entries, on a tablet of KH Scribe 1 that counts VIR+*307 2 on the next line (GORILA III 45). KH 82 .4 ]*336[, dotted and broken at both sides (III 97), is not counted.

GORILA's countermark, alone on the nodule HT Wa 1854, one of A 365–370 on HT Wa 1849–1854 (Salgarella 2020, 309–12). The corpus also has it on HT 49a .6, *370 1 between A-RU 1 and *312 1, which SigLA leaves unread and Salgarella does not list: the transcription draws a dotted sign there, a flag on a staff (GORILA I 93), and the sign index has 370 on HT Wa 1854 alone (V 310).

On the Akrotiri jug THE Zb 5 JE stands by itself, incised before firing, with nothing to read it by.

KH 1 is no second token: the edition prints ]JE · GRA+F 70[, the tablet broken at the left before JE (GORILA III 23), so the sign ends a word whose beginning is lost. Khania has two more words ending in JE, RI-TA-JE before CYP+D on KH 6 and ]-JE 1 on KH 50.

GORILA's A 611, OLE with QI, at TY 3a.2, .4 and TY 3b.2. Salgarella asks whether it is a sign of its own, the two parts hard to see, though the tablet's many OLE ligatures favour OLE with QI (Salgarella 2020, 146).

Alone twice on HT 126b. Linear B *87 twe: Davis takes it for a sign Linear B borrowed from Linear A with the same or a very similar value, and leaves /tʷ/ out of his inventory for want of a syllabic use (2026b, 95–96 n. 385, 154 n. 579). Linear B writes twe only at Knossos, in o-da-twe-ta, and for Salgarella 'it cannot be excluded' that Linear A had an ancestor of it in the sign of HT 126b .2–3, which GORILA V therefore sets among the AB signs, p. xlii (2020, 39 and n. 105); her later chapter counts twe among the complex signs Linear B introduced (2023, 411). Del Freo's current phonographic signary of Linear A leaves AB 87 out (Petrakis and Salgarella 2026, 31, Fig. 0.1, after Del Freo 2023, 81). No reading.
GORILA's A 588, the wine sign with TE inside it, cut on the pithos KN Zb 34 (Pierini 2022, 46–47, fig. 3.8a) and on the pithos rim THE Zb 13.
ZA 1a ZA 5, after NI 42½. On KH 22 .1 ]-ZA ends a lost word, with ]SI-ZA possible (GORILA III 55).

Alone on KH 57.2, apparently before a numeral in a damaged context, probably a logogram (Salgarella 2020, 157, 170, 314); Melena takes AB 20 for the ancestor of Linear B zo (Melena 2014a, 8, apud Salgarella 2020, 170 n. 96). On the Akrotiri ostracon THE Zg 5 ZO is one of the single signs before quantities taken for abbreviations of Minoan textile names (Michailidou 1992–1993; Boulotis 1998; Burke 2010, 49, apud Nosch and Weilhartner 2026, 131). Linear B writes ZO on its cloth sign, a ligature that 'perhaps appears in Linear A. The identity of the word abbreviated to ZO is unknown' (Killen 2024, 724). Del Freo's phonographic signary of Linear A leaves AB 20 out (Petrakis and Salgarella 2026, 31, Fig. 0.1).

HT 11a .4–5, counted 3, and HT 93a .5–6, counted 6: the man sign and I side by side in the word column, with no divider, GORILA's 100/102-28 (V 272). On HT 93a the two entries above it end on a divider and I before GRA+PA, A-SE · I GRA+PA 26 ¾ and QA-QA-RU · I GRA+PA 5 (I 147), so the man sign stands where the recipient stands and I is the lexicon's I 'ration'. On HT 11a two short strokes project from the man sign's right side (I 23).
KH 82 .3 ]*315, then 1 and the break: the tabular copy sets ] before the sign and the drawing none, with 'trace à droite' (GORILA III 97). It stands in the column of words, counted 1.

on_file.value: TI (CANDIDATE), the Phaistos MM II form of AB37

entries.note: A ring on a Λ in GORILA's drawings. It also opens *320-NA (PH 16a) and is doubled in *320-*320-MA (PH Wc 40), each counted with its word.
A logogram alone on HT 93a.7 (Salgarella 2020, 309–12).

A transaction sign alone on HT 122b.1 (Salgarella 2020, 309–12): JE-DI · *346 · and the man sign at the break, the sign a tall upright with a narrow closed foot to its right (GORILA I 209). The sign index has it here alone, as a transaction sign, [3] (V 304).

KH 6 .3, after ]KI-SA-NE CYP+D ½: *347, two short strokes detached from it and the break (GORILA III 27). The same hand draws *306 with two such strokes at its side (KH 6 .7, KH 11 .3 and .6), and the fraction on KH 11 as a wedge with them.

Davis lists *348 among the Linear A signs that look syllabic and have no Linear B counterpart (Davis 2026b, 96 n. 387); Salgarella has A 348 only inside the composite A 647 on KH 11.3, its use unclear (Salgarella 2020, 318). KH 11 .3 has *348 alone before CYP with two fractions, and .6 SI in the same column before CYP with the same amount (GORILA III 39).

KH 100 .1 *352 *306[, under a lost upper edge. Its editors, who publish the tablet as KH 99, read the sign tentatively: the curved crossing strokes could be a variant of DE, unusually large, or A 352, 'found once on the roundel KH Wc 2100'; the second sign is incomplete too (Andreadaki-Vlasaki and Hallager 2007, 12). They take *352 for a syllable in both places (2007, 17). On KH Wc 2100 it stands inside VIR+[?]-*352-JA.
GORILA's countermark, alone on the nodule HT Wa 1849, one of A 365–370 on HT Wa 1849–1854 (Salgarella 2020, 309–12).
GORILA's countermark, alone on the nodule HT Wa 1850, one of A 365–370 on HT Wa 1849–1854 (Salgarella 2020, 309–12).
GORILA's countermark, alone on the nodule HT Wa 1851, one of A 365–370 on HT Wa 1849–1854 (Salgarella 2020, 309–12).
GORILA's countermark, alone on the nodule HT Wa 1852, one of A 365–370 on HT Wa 1849–1854 (Salgarella 2020, 309–12).
GORILA's countermark, alone on the nodule HT Wa 1853, one of A 365–370 on HT Wa 1849–1854 (Salgarella 2020, 309–12).
GORILA A 654, 404VAS+08 (GORILA V 312): MA 10b .2, a tapering cup with a loop handle at its left and A written inside, counted 2.
HT 31: a plain tapering vessel on a short foot.

No token of the sign alone survives whole. MA 10c ends on 414VAS[ ], a loop handle and the left of a rounded body at the break (GORILA V 51, 314). MA 10d has the vessel twice with a sign inside, *414+F and *414+[ ].

GORILA A 655, 405VAS+Ω (GORILA V 312): MA 10b .1, a tapering cup with a loop handle at each side and a sign inside it. Nearest among the Linear B vessels is *212, u-do-ro, 'a conical bucket-shaped bowl with two horizontal (?) handles' (Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 324, 328).
HT 93a: a branched outline with curled ends; the vessel shape is not clear.

HT 31 .1, the first vessel of the list: a bowl on three legs with two loops standing on the rim (GORILA V 313). The ivory ring KN Zg 57 has a tripod among the vessels of face A, one of the two vase signs there with no syllabogram above it; the editors point to HT 31 for the shape (Kanta, Nakassis, Palaima and Perna 2024, 38). Linear B *201, ti-ri-po 'tripod', has the same bowl, three legs and two loops on the rim (Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 324–325); *409-VS has the legs with no handles and *411-VS two bars at the sides (GORILA V 313).

GORILA A 657, 407VAS+08 (GORILA V 312): HT 39 .5, after KU-RO and counted 100, a broad shallow vessel with a raised loop at each end of the rim and A above its middle. Nearest among the Linear B vessels is *200, pi-je-ra₃ 'boiling-pan', 'a large shallow vessel … provided with high-swung handles' (Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 324–325).

GORILA A 663, 417VAS 'L2' (GORILA V 315, 322): PH 8a .1, counted 7, the hatched vessel of KH Wc 2006 and 2007 with the fraction sign L2 beneath it, as *418+L2 has on .3. The Phaistos drawing is broader than the Khania one, with a flat bottom and parallel strokes for the lattice (GORILA I 296; III 116).

GORILA A 505, 04+02: HT 104 .1 TA-PA · TE+RO ·, between two dividers in the heading. The editors' note: TE and RO 'with the two horizontal strokes running together' (GORILA I 171); the sign index lists it under 02 and under 04 (V 145, 151).

The contribution of capital, TE 'contribution' with RO 'principal', under TA-PA 'partners', heading three shares that sum to 95. Akk. kasap tappūti is 'partnership capital' (CAD T 192), and qaqqadu 'head' is the 'original amount, principal' of a loan (CAD Q 109), as RO is rōš 'head'.
GORILA A 648: the footed cup 400VAS with a sign above its rim, read 400VAS+RI with the RI dotted, or 400VAS+E with the fraction sign (GORILA V 311, 318). HT 110b .1, counted 3.

THE 12, a fragment from Akrotiri Δ18: SigLA codes its one sign AB 22f, the she-goat; Younger reads ]OLE[. The drawing has a short bar, a diagonal under it and a long stem bowed to the left, three strokes that do not join; the photograph held shows no more. Neither reading is confirmed.

HT 133: A-DU · TE GRA+DA 55, the grain sign carrying DA after TE. Under the same heading A-DU, HT 86a and HT 95b spell DA-ME before grain (DA-ME GRA+B 20; DA-ME 10), and HT 120 has DA-ME GRA+K+L 74: DA is the first sign of DA-ME, as Linear B TELA+PA carries the first sign of pa-wo (Melena 2014, 143). One occurrence; HT 133 is the work of another scribe than HT 86a and HT 120. See DA-ME.

THE 7a, Akrotiri Δ18: before 46 stands a sign with a curved head, three strokes descending from it and a baseline beneath, the sheep sign; SigLA codes it AB 21f, the ewe, and Younger reads OVIS with no mark of sex. The sign before the first numeral survives as two upright remnants, which SigLA leaves unread and Younger reads OVIS again. The photograph and drawing held do not settle the mark of sex.

GORILA's A 540, a hapax on KN 28b .3, classed as SU+MI. Salgarella holds that it 'may be better interpreted' as SU+OLE, her SU+OIL: the second element has the shape OLE takes in A 622 (OLE+MI), which would otherwise read MI+MI, and MI binds only to OLE there and to one unidentified sign in A 634 (2020, 145). GORILA's drawing shows a stem with short ticks at its top beside SU, with no bowl or dot (I 263).

The pig sign with SI set above it and RE beside it, on a livestock tablet, a sign GORILA does not number (Salgarella 2020, 147–48). It may answer Linear B SUS+SI, though the value of SI may have changed (Salgarella 2020, 148), Linear B's pig with si standing for 'fattened pig' (Salgarella 2023, 396, after Meissner 2019). Meissner weighs reading it si-au-re beside Mycenaean si-a₂-ro (PY Cn 608) (Meissner 2019, apud Salgarella 2020, 148 n. 70).

The cloth sign AB 54 with SE inscribed, 200 counted (Boulotis 2008, 77, 80). Linear B *168+SE stands only in the latest Knossos archive and 'might be a textile' (Nosch 2024, 333); Davaras 1986 and Firth 2016, 235 'do not interpret *168 as a textile' (in Nosch 2024, 333 n. 72). Melena's weaver's vessel, the kalathiskos, Duhoux rejects: *168 lies on its long side, the kalathiskoi stand on the short one (Melena 1975, 118–134, in Duhoux 1977, 658).
GORILA A 598 (GORILA III 25): KH 5 .2, the wine sign with WI, counted 2, between WI-SA-SA-NE with CYP+E 2 and WI-NA-DU.

Heads HT 101, before GRA+QE 40 and three oil entries; SA-RA₂ heads the next section. The goat sign *22F stands between ZU and DI, so no run of two syllabic signs is left. Salgarella notes that in Linear A only the gendered variant AB 22f is also used as a syllabogram (2020, 214), and Del Freo's phonographic signary lists AB 22f (Petrakis and Salgarella 2026, 31, Fig. 0.1, after Del Freo 2023, 81); Davis's Linear A grid sets AB 22 at pi₂, unconfirmed (2026b, 18, Table 1.3). Read as a syllabogram, AB 22f makes ZU-*22F-DI a word of three syllabic signs. It stands among the names as a personal name of unknown affiliation, and HT 101 is translated with it as an opaque heading. No reading.

HT 128b .1, two signs before GRA+KU 1, the vessel bracketed and dotted; a fracture crosses the first sign (GORILA I 221). GORILA's sign index files the pair as 21f-329 (V 176) and has no HT 128b under the man sign (V 272); SigLA reads AB100-A329. On the edition's own drawing the first sign has two lower strokes ending in bent feet, as the man sign has.
PH 12a, before 10 and fractions; a fracture crosses the last sign.
